title: Impact of Surprise Tariff Announcements on Industry Returns

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
To estimate the impact of surprise tariff announcements on industry returns, we will employ an Event Study method. This approach allows us to quantify the abnormal returns of stocks around the event date, which in this case is the surprise tariff announcement. The key assumption of the event study method is that the market model holds, meaning that the expected return of a stock is a function of the market return and the stock's beta. We also assume that the event (surprise tariff announcement) is unexpected and that there are no other significant events occurring around the same time that could affect the stock returns.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load necessary libraries
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

# Read the dataset
data <- read_csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s66_data.csv")

# Calculate abnormal returns (AR) for each stock on each day
data <- data %>%
  mutate(AR = ret - (beta * mkt_ret))

# Calculate cumulative abnormal returns (CAR) around the event day
data_car <- data %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(CAR = sum(AR))

# Calculate the average CAR for all stocks on the event day
average_car <- data %>%
  filter(event_day == 0) %>%
  summarise(avg_AR = mean(AR))

# Print the average abnormal return on the event day
print(paste("Average abnormal return on the event day: ", average_car$avg_AR))

# Perform a basic robustness check: calculate the CAR for different event windows
data_1day_car <- data %>%
  filter(event_day >= -1 & event_day <= 1) %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(CAR_1day = sum(AR))

data_3day_car <- data %>%
  filter(event_day >= -3 & event_day <= 3) %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(CAR_3day = sum(AR))

data_5day_car <- data %>%
  filter(event_day >= -5 & event_day <= 5) %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(CAR_5day = sum(AR))

# Calculate the average CAR for different event windows
avg_1day_car <- mean(data_1day_car$CAR_1day)
avg_3day_car <- mean(data_3day_car$CAR_3day)
avg_5day_car <- mean(data_5day_car$CAR_5day)

# Print the results of the robustness checks
print(paste("Average CAR for 1-day window: ", avg_1day_car))
print(paste("Average CAR for 3-day window: ", avg_3day_car))
print(paste("Average CAR for 5-day window: ", avg_5day_car))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
We expect the average abnormal return on the event day to be negative, as surprise tariff announcements are likely to have a negative impact on the stock returns of companies in industries exposed to international trade. The magnitude of the effect will depend on the severity of the tariff announcement and the level of exposure of the industry to international trade. We expect the average CAR for different event windows to be negative as well, with the magnitude of the effect increasing as the event window expands. This is because the negative impact of the tariff announcement may take some time to materialize and be reflected in the stock returns. The exact magnitude of the effect will depend on the specifics of the data and the event.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Leverage the event-day variation around the surprise announcement.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The surprise tariff announcement led to a significant decrease in CAR for exposed industries.
